questions.stem: At night, a plant releases more carbon dioxide than it absorbs. Why is this?

options.text: Plants only respire at night and do not respire during the day
Photosynthesis cannot occur without light, so only respiration produces CO2
Stomata are fully open at night, allowing more CO2 to escape
The rate of respiration increases significantly in darkness

questions.explanation: Plants respire all the time (day and night), producing CO2. During the day, photosynthesis uses up more CO2 than respiration produces. At night, photosynthesis stops because there is no light, so the CO2 produced by respiration is released as a net output.
